summary: The update_link method now computes style._link_id by appending the hash of the (pickled) meta data to a value taken from a global _id_generator that yields successive integers (next(_id_generator)), instead of appending a random six‑digit integer from randint(0, 999999). Consequently, for any given call where a link (or meta) is present, the resulting _link_id is deterministic and increases monotonically with each invocation, whereas previously it varied randomly each time. When no link or meta is supplied, _link_id remains an empty string, unchanged.

summary: When bump_build is invoked on a Version whose build metadata is either None or a string without any digits, the method now appends ".0" to the build string (e.g., turning an empty build into +.0 or "build" into "build.0"), whereas previously it left such build metadata unchanged. fix(next_version): reset prerelease when token changes (#339)
summary: When next_version is called with part="prerelease" and a non‑None prerelease_token, if the version already has a prerelease whose first token (the part before the first dot) differs from prerelease_token, the method now returns a version whose prerelease is set to "<prerelease_token>.1" and whose build is cleared, instead of incrementing the existing prerelease number. In all other cases (no prerelease, or the token matches), the behavior remains unchanged.

title: Fix string_to_int radix when alphabet_index is provided
summary: When an alphabet_index is supplied, string_to_int now computes the radix as len(alphabet_index) instead of len(alphabet), so the base used for conversion changes whenever the two lengths differ. Consequently, inputs such as "010" with alphabet ['0','1','2'] and index {'0':0,'1':1} yield 2 instead of 3, and "20" with alphabet ['0','1'] and index {'0':0,'1':1,'2':2} yield 6 instead of 4.

title: fix: Improve randomness (#101)
summary: For a call such as ShortUUID().random(length=1) the function previously returned a single‑character string derived from a random hex value (e.g., '4'), whereas after the change it returns a single character chosen directly from the alphabet (e.g., 'a'). In general, the method now generates each character independently with secrets.choice(self._alphabet) instead of converting a random integer to the alphabet, so its output differs for the same input.

summary: The function now unconditionally calls self.wait(retry_state) and assigns the result to retry_state.upcoming_sleep. Previously, when self.wait was falsy (e.g., None, False, 0, or an empty list), the function skipped the call and set upcoming_sleep to 0.0. After the change, those same inputs cause a TypeError because the non‑callable value is invoked as a function, while callable wait objects continue to behave as before.

title: fix nonpositive item limits in constrained_batches

witnesses.after: ValueError: maximum count must be greater than zero
ValueError: maximum count must be greater than zero

summary: When a non‑None max_count argument that is zero or negative is supplied, constrained_batches now raises ValueError: maximum count must be greater than zero instead of producing batches; previously it ignored the invalid max_count and returned a single batch containing all items (or an empty batch for an empty iterable). For example, list(constrained_batches(['a','b','c','d','e'],10,max_count=0)) changed from [('a','b','c','d','e')] to raising the exception, and list(constrained_batches([],5,max_count=0)) changed from [] to raising the same exception.

Fix humanize reporting 'a month' for 16-day differences
summary: The change prevents rounding up to a month when the elapsed time is more than two weeks but less than a full month and no calendar month has fully passed; instead, it returns a weeks‑based description. Consequently, Arrow(2020,1,1).humanize(Arrow(2020,1,20)) now yields '2 weeks ago' rather than 'a month ago'.
